transcript.text: This could be as simple as a flat battery/charging or plug issue, a blockage causing it to overheat and cut out, or less commonly a motor fault. Is it completely dead, or does it switch on but have no suction and/or the brush bar does not turn? Before checking anything, switch it off and unplug it or remove the battery; if it stopped after getting hot, leave it for 30 minutes to cool before trying again.
its completely dead, mine plugs into the wall. nothing happens when i switch it on. it stopped while i was doing the stairs

Start with the mains supply side: the socket, plug fuse or cable are more likely than the motor. Unplug the vacuum first. Try another appliance in the same socket; then inspect the vacuum cable and plug for damage or heat marks. If it has a standard UK fused plug, you can fit a known-good 13A fuse while unplugged. If the socket works and the cable/plug look sound but it remains dead after an hour cooled down, an internal switch, cable connection or thermal cut-out is likely and it will need an engineer rather than further dismantling.

the lamp works in the socket. theres black tape on the cable near the plug, my son did it ages ago, its a bit bent there. once it came on for a second when i moved the wire but then went off again. i havent got a screwdriver or spare fuse

Do not use it again or keep bending/moving that cable. The taped, bent section near the plug and the fact it briefly came on when the wire was moved make a broken wire or loose connection there very likely; tape is not a safe repair for a mains lead. The socket itself is fine, so this is unlikely to be a motor problem. It needs a proper replacement lead/plug repair by a vacuum repairer or qualified electrician, or replacement of the vacuum if that is uneconomical. Do not try to open the plug or fit a fuse without the right tools.

candidates: Blocked filter, hose or floorhead causing thermal cut-out (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "stopped working". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
